input.title: Refund visible in the account
input.request: I can see my outgoing transfer to Northmere Home Supplies in my secure portal. The supplier told me it might return the £42.80, but I cannot tell whether that specific refund has reached my account. Please check the incoming entries and confirm its status.

events.text: Outgoing transfer — Northmere Home Supplies — £42.80 — shown in account history.

I am escalating this because Northmere Home Supplies said the £42.80 might be returned. Please check whether the incoming entry is for that specific transfer; I do not want it confused with another payment.
I am checking the linked incoming entries on Elowen Marr's account for a £42.80 refund matching the Northmere Home Supplies transfer. I will not treat a similar-looking entry as a match.

summary: Elowen Marr, on secure chat and not yet verified, asked the desk to check whether an incoming £42.80 entry relates to her specific transfer to Northmere Home Supplies, which had said it might be returned. The desk asked the incoming-payments system and closed the case as waiting, since that system's answer is not yet in; a second attempt to ask it was refused because the check was already on record and the case was in a waiting state. No action was taken and no refund has been confirmed or matched, so what remains is the incoming result, or a person picking up the case.

request_type.instructions: What does the customer want from the bank now?

criteria.question: something the bank's records can answer (a status, a reason, a detail, a statement, a report), even if the customer may want something changed afterwards
criteria.register: a dispute, a review, a return, or the correction of a record that is wrong, for a team to look into
criteria.change: a change the customer chooses to an instruction, a mandate or the profile (a new amount, date, phone or address)
criteria.instruction: an instruction to act now (block a card, cancel a payment or a mandate, revoke a role)
criteria.access: signing in, a PIN, a password, recovery of access
criteria.authority: something only another person may approve or give (a second signatory, an administrator, a new user's access)
criteria.unknown: The text does not say, or says too little to tell.

criteria.transfer: an outgoing transfer or payment the customer made, or a payment instruction
criteria.incoming_payment: money expected into the customer's account, or a refund to it
criteria.standing_order: a standing order or a recurring payment instruction
criteria.direct_debit: a Direct Debit mandate or collection
criteria.card: a card itself (replacement, dispatch, block, restriction, PIN)
criteria.card_payment: a card purchase or card payment attempt
criteria.batch: an uploaded payment or payroll file, or a row in it
criteria.payment_package: a payment package waiting for signatories
criteria.profile: the customer's profile details (name, phone, address)
criteria.access: signing in, devices, sessions, password recovery
criteria.document: an export, a report or a bank confirmation document
criteria.fee: a fee or charge applied by the bank
criteria.role: a user's role or access in a company profile
criteria.unknown: The text does not say, or says too little to tell.

A bank's service desk (Harrow & Vale Bank, fictional). The bank never acts or approves for someone else, never handles a PIN or a password, and never claims more than a record shows.

The case stops at one moment: choose the bank's next step from here with one tool, then stop. The facts are what the desk read from the bank's records; a fact not listed is not known yet. I tried to ask the incoming system again and the desk refused, because that check is already on record and the case is in a waiting state.

So far nothing shows that a refund has arrived, and the case doesn't say which entry would match your original transfer. I won't tie any incoming entry to that transfer until the record shows it. Your identity also isn't verified on this chat yet, which may limit what can be shared once the result is in.

I'm taking no further action now. The case stays open until the incoming result comes back or a person picks it up.
